public_rationale: Reporting supports the qualitative reading that operators supplied the main interactive judgment at We Robot. Tesla confirms human assistance and autonomous locomotion. No source measures the share of 'commonsense' numerically.
limitations: Support depends on identifying We Robot as the intended demonstration.
The task-level account relies on reputable reporting; Tesla's statement describes assistance less specifically.
The evidence does not support a claim that every function was teleoperated.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: In recent Optimus demonstrations, all or most of the required commonsense was apparently supplied by human teleoperators.

statement.excerpt: In Elon Musk’s recent Optimus demonstrations, all or most of the commonsense required was apparently outsourced to human teleoperators.
statement.document_title: AI still lacks “common” sense, 70 years later

from_speaker: all or most of the commonsense required
our_interpretation: The likely referent is the late-2024 public demonstrations, especially the October 10 We Robot event.
The ordinary reading concerns the main interactive judgments displayed in conversation, serving guests and responding to them. It does not imply that every motor movement was remotely controlled.
'Apparently' qualifies the confidence of the observation; it is not a conditional antecedent.
The target period is the final quarter of 2024, immediately preceding the post. Support from We Robot cannot automatically be extended to every demonstration in that quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Credible records show human operators supplying the main interactive judgment at the relevant demonstration, while any autonomous functions are identified.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible records show that the main interactive judgments were performed autonomously, with human intervention only peripheral.
